Hey, my name is Kyle Warner.
I'm a professional mountain bike racer and I took the Pfizer vaccine.
My second dose was on June 10th and about a month later I developed pericarditis,
which is swelling of the liner of the heart, as well as POTS and reactive arthritis.
It's brought an end to my career as I know it and a lot of my just day-to-day life has changed drastically.
So we're out here at this event just kind of speaking out on vaccine injury
and trying to get some acceptance from people that this is a real issue
and that we're not trying to cause any drama or that we're fake in any way.
We just want to try to get acceptance and know that this is a real thing,
get some acknowledgments so we can have an honest discussion as a country.
Because I believe where there is risk, there must be choice.
And the fact that they're hiding the risk from us and, you know,
I got coerced into doing this, doing my part and was injured from the vaccine.
And yeah, just trying to help other people not make the same mistake.
The controversial vaccine mandates that have undoubtedly helped increase vaccination rates
are sparking warnings and lawsuits across the country.
We take a look at Los Angeles County, New York State, Pennsylvania,
and possible disruptions at airports due to Biden's vaccine mandate.
The Los Angeles County Sheriff is voicing concerns over the effects of the area's vaccine mandate.
Sheriff Alex Villanueva says about 100 staff or 20 percent have already filed for early retirement.
They're the experts in so many different capacities.
Homicide investigators, crisis negotiators, senior patrolmen.
I mean, all kinds of different positions these people occupy.
And these are the people that are starting to walk away.
L.A. County employees are required to be fully vaccinated by October 1st.
Villanueva said some of his employees would rather be fired than get the shot.
Three New York nurses are marching to the Supreme Court to contest the state's vaccine mandate.
They've objected to taking a COVID-19 vaccine due to their religious beliefs.
Specifically, they don't agree with the use of aborted fetal cells used in testing.
This after a federal appellate court allowed the mandate to stay.
One of the attorneys for the plaintiffs calls New York's mandate blatant religious discrimination.
NTD reached out to Governor Hochul's office for comment.
Former Governor Cuomo required health care workers to get the shot to combat the spread of the Delta variant.
Over in Pennsylvania, a lawsuit alleges that the vaccine mandate violates constitutional rights.
It alleges taking or declining a vaccine is a political act.
Therefore, when employers force it on employees, they're forcing them to engage in political speech,
which is a violation of the First Amendment.
Governor Tom Wolf's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment,
but Pennsylvania has mandated the vaccine for health care workers,
saying it's important to protect vulnerable people in health care facilities.
I have limited time. Let me just ask you something else.
What percent of CDC employees are vaccinated?
We're actively encouraging vaccination in all of our employees and doing a lot of education and outreach
in order to get our agency fully vaccinated.
I don't have that for you today.
I'm told that 75, some north of 75 percent of CDC employees at headquarters are still working remotely.
We are following regulations through HHS and the federal government.
No, that's not my question. I apologize to be rude, but I'm asking a very straightforward question.
I've been told that north of 75 percent of employees at CDC headquarters are working remotely.
Senator, I don't actually know the number off the top of my head.
Okay, when you look down the hallway, are there empty desks?
Are over 50 percent of the desks empty?
Senator, I don't have the numbers off the top of my head.
What I will tell you is that we're working closely within HHS and the administration to follow the governmental rules for return to the work.
There was a recent GAO report that shows and released in the last two weeks that there's been no coordinated response in the federal government to get people back into work.
Now, if there's any agency that since we have teachers in Fulton County are back at work, that the caseload of COVID in Fulton County is about 88 at its peak, it was 606.
If what I've been told by someone who frankly kind of knows that people in laboratories are not showing up.
I have no clue how people, how laboratory workers who presumably are vaccinated wearing PPE would consider themselves eligible to stay at home.
So I got my third dose of the Pfizer booster vaccine on Sunday.
And on Monday, by about 1030 in the morning, I was having body aches and pains and chills and stuff.
Then that night, I could not stay awake.
I was having fevers, still the chills, still the body aches.
But by the afternoon, I thought I was doing pretty good.
Woke up this morning and I have sores all inside my mouth.
The fever is back. I still have the body aches.
As much as I love my shots, I fucking hate the side effects.
